source: Agriculture Sector Development Project (ASDP), ADB Loan No. 2023-CAM(SF), Guide No.1: Coconut-damaging beetle and protective measures, prepared by Kampot Province Department of Agricultural Extension, 2008
text:
Besides the introduced Asecodes hispinarum wasp, the guide lists other naturally occurring beneficial organisms found on coconut palms that help suppress the beetle population and that farmers are told to protect rather than kill with broad-spectrum pesticide: weaver ants (អង្រែង), earwigs (សត្វខ្នុយពីរ), geckos/small lizards observed hunting on coconut fronds, and bacteria and other insect groups that also help destroy beetle larvae on the leaves.

The guide also describes hand-picking (ការចាប់ចោលដៃ) as a simple mechanical control method — physically removing and destroying visible adult beetles and larvae from young leaves by hand, useful for light infestations or backyard trees where chemical or biological control is impractical.

Risks of chemical control are flagged separately: pesticide cost, drift/harm to non-target crops, damage risk to different coconut varieties, and harm to the environment and human health are all listed as drawbacks of relying on chemical insecticide as the main control method, reinforcing the guide's preference for the biological (wasp-based) approach combined with hand-picking and protection of natural predators.
